questions.question: Describe the main stages of the negotiations from 1990 to 1993.
questions.expected_answer: Groote Schuur and Pretoria Minutes; National Peace Accord September 1991. CODESA 1, 20 December 1991, World Trade Centre Kempton Park, 19 parties, Declaration of Intent; CP, PAC, AZAPO stayed away. Potchefstroom by-election; white referendum 17 March 1992, about 69% yes. CODESA 2 May 1992 deadlock over majorities, minority veto vs majority rule. Record of Understanding 26 September 1992; Slovo's sunset clauses (GNU five years, civil service jobs, amnesty). Multi-Party Negotiating Process April 1993, 26 parties; election date 27 April 1994; interim constitution November 1993 (Bill of Rights, Constitutional Court, nine provinces, constitutional principles); Transitional Executive Council.

questions.question: Explain the political violence of 1990 to 1994.
questions.expected_answer: About 14 000 dead. ANC-IFP conflict in Natal and Witwatersrand; hostels; train attacks; third force; Inkathagate 1991; Goldstone and TRC evidence of security force involvement; ANC killings too. Boipatong 17 June 1992, KwaMadala hostel, about 45 killed, ANC withdrew, rolling mass action. Bisho 7 September 1992, Ciskei Defence Force, 28 marchers and a soldier killed; Gqozo. Chris Hani killed 10 April 1993 (Waluś, Derby-Lewis), Afrikaner neighbour, Mandela's call for calm. AWB at WTC June 1993; St James Church 25 July 1993 (APLA, 11 killed); Amy Biehl August 1993. 1994: Freedom Alliance; Bophuthatswana crisis, Mangope removed, AWB members shot; Viljoen and Freedom Front; Shell House 28 March 1994; IFP joined 19 April; right-wing bombs.

questions.question: Describe the 1994 election and its results.
questions.expected_answer: 26-29 April 1994 (26 special votes, 27 main day); nearly 20 million voted; long queues; IEC under Kriegler; problems but substantially free and fair. ANC 62.65% (252 seats), NP 20.39% (82), IFP 10.54% (43); FF, DP, PAC, ACDP; ANC won 7 provinces, NP Western Cape, IFP KwaZulu-Natal. GNU; Mandela inaugurated 10 May 1994 at Union Buildings; Deputy Presidents Mbeki and De Klerk; "Never, never and never again"; Nobel Peace Prize 1993. Final Constitution signed at Sharpeville 10 December 1996. Freedom Day 27 April.
